scope.summary: This standard specifies the physical, chemical, biological, and performance-testing requirements for disposable (non-reusable) baby diapers intended for external use. It establishes guidelines for sizing, absorbency, raw material safety, and hygienic manufacturing to ensure comfort, protection, and skin-friendliness for newborns, infants, and toddlers.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all disposable baby diapers must conform to IS 17509:2021 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified baby diapers in India is a punishable criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small units are granted specific delayed implementation phases, and products manufactured by Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to disposable baby diapers.

requirements.detail: Every commercial pack of disposable baby diapers must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to verify conformity.

Disposable baby diapers must consist of three primary layers to ensure moisture isolation: a) top cover or top sheet (for skin contact comfort); b) absorbent core (middle layer featuring superabsorbent polymers, cellulose pulp, or tissue to retain liquid); and c) outer protective barrier or back sheet (leak-proof layer to prevent liquid pass-through).

Under Amendment No. 3, the weight classification range for the corresponding variety in Table 1, Sl No. (v), is substituted as '9 kg to 13 kg' (originally defined as '9 kg to 11 kg' in earlier amendments). Other varieties include New Born (2 to 5 kg), Small (3 to 8 kg), and Medium (6 to 11 kg).
For premature babies and other specialized varieties not covered in Table 1, the recommended dimensions and tolerances are declared by the manufacturer for reference only.
The actual physical dimensions of baby diapers can vary based on the specific product design chosen by the manufacturer.

Diaper raw materials must undergo biocompatibility evaluation under Clause 7.4 (including cytotoxicity, skin irritation, and skin sensitization tests) once for existing raw material and whenever there is a change in the supply source. The finished product must maintain a skin-friendly pH value.
To prevent infections on sensitive infant skin, the diaper must satisfy strict limits on total bacterial and fungal count. Common pathogens like Staphylococcus aureus must be completely absent.

To prevent hormonal and toxic hazards to infants, the total individual or combined phthalate plasticizer content in raw materials or finished products must be strictly limited (typically less than 0.1 percent) when tested in accordance with IS 9873 (Part 6).

The composite diaper assembly must pass mandatory physical absorbency tests, including Rate of Absorption (speed of liquid draw-in), Rewet under Load (minimal fluid return to the skin under infant body weight to keep the skin dry), and Minimum Total Absorption Capacity.
The diapers must feature secure, adjustable, and skin-safe adhesive or hook-and-loop fasteners that do not restrict movement or scratch the infant.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17509 : 2021 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification regulating disposable (non-reusable) baby diapers sold or imported in India. Under the statutory Medical Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all baby diapers supplied to the Indian market must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). It outlines strict raw material checks, including biocompatibility (testing for cytotoxicity, skin irritation, and sensitization) and a maximum phthalate limit of 0.1 percent to protect infants from plasticizer toxicity. It classifies diapers based on weight ranges from New Born up to Extra Large. Amendment No. 3 (February 2025) modifies the weight range for the corresponding variety under Sl No. (v) to '9 kg to 13 kg' (originally 9 to 11 kg) [1]. It also notes that dimensions for premature babies are to be declared by the manufacturer for reference only [1]. This standard ensures that baby diapers provide excellent leak-proof retention, high rate of absorption, and minimal rewet under load, while keeping infants safe from harmful pathogens, extreme pH levels, and industrial chemicals.
